exact_missing_items: But `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` still has owner-level drift in the same file:
Each failed node attempt must leave a structured receipt/handoff artifact containing: what it did, what changed, why failed, what to try next — this is mandatory, not optional

Governing layer design: deterministic scheduler/state machine (not one long-running super-agent); bounded worker/reviewer/remediation agents with explicit context windows; lightweight planning/replan agent only at graph-construction or graph-patch boundaries

Highest-pressure docs for condensation are `Plans/storage-plan.md`, `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`, `Plans/Models_System.md`, `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md`, `Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md`, `Plans/Crosswalk.md`, and `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md`.
Issue classes requiring corroboration (5): missing wiring, implementation quality concerns, unmet intent despite passing tests, missing spec/hidden dependency, graph structure insufficiency
Plans/Models_System.md model selection must become lane-aware — models must be selectable/overridable per lane context
Revocation and reopen labels must be: Promotion Revoked, Seam Completion Revoked, Reopened, Reopened by Patch, Reopened by New Evidence
Seam review outputs must include: verdict, failure classes with severity, evidence bundle/rationale, remediation-node or graph-patch recommendation, corroboration requirement and outcome
Seam-level acceptance dimensions (5): operability, state coherence, workflow completeness, UX coherence, architectural coherence
`Plans/Contracts_V0.md` and `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md` already carry `startup_recovered` in runtime wake canon.
gap_candidates.blocking_reason: Concrete Plans/** document requires content reconciliation vs transfer obligation.
